attributes.mlflow.spanOutputs: {"answer": "**What's wrong** Two things stand out even though the measured LCP (76ms) is fine: the LCP image is a 1,043,802-byte PNG loaded with no priority hint, and `print.css` is marked render-blocking with no `media` attribute — so it delays first paint for every visitor even though it only applies when printing. **Who it affects** This test ran on localhost with near-zero network latency, so the 76ms number won't hold on a real connection — a 1MB image fetched over an actual network, without being prioritized, will push LCP well past the "good" 2500ms threshold. The unscoped `print.css` adds blocking time for everyone, on every load, for a stylesheet almost nobody needs at page-load time. **The fix** ```html ``` Also worth compressing/re-encoding `hero-riverfront.png` — 1MB for a 1200×500 hero image is large regardless of network speed. **Watch out** No WCAG success criterion applies here — this is a performance recommendation, not a conformance failure, and as measured (76ms) your LCP already passes the "good" threshold. Treat this as risk-reduction for real-world users, not a required fix. Don't add `loading="lazy"` to this image — it's the LCP element and should load eagerly; lazy-loading it would make things worse, not better.", "tool_calls": 0}
